attributes.residual:
DEFECT 1, boss.c: the definition is `f32 Random(f32 scale)` in src/game/ps2/ml_fmath.c and eight TUs declare it that way, but boss.c declared `extern f64 Random(f64 a)`. All nine `Random(0.1f)` call sites in BossSpewCoins therefore widened the argument and loaded the f64 0x3FB99999A0000000 where retail loads the f32 0x3DCCCCCD -- nine wrong-width pool references. combat.c had the return half of the same defect. The value passed is numerically the same, so this is a CODEGEN defect rather than a behavioural one, and it is worth a score: real 137 -> 121, fuzzy +2.89.
DEFECT 2, items.c, GAMEPLAY: at +0x194 of update_player_milestone (123/123, real 46) retail emits `lwz r4,0(0) @lbl_80344800(EMB_SDA21)` and we emitted `lwz r4,0(0) @sShownMilestones(EMB_SDA21)`. lbl_80344800 (.sbss 0x80344800) is the free-running frame counter that gamemain.c and sysservice.c increment; sShownMilestones is 0x803448F4. The instruction words are identical, so every arbiter read the function as unchanged. The loop tests bit i of that word to decide MBTreeClearFlags against MBTreeSetFlags on each of five milestone icons: retail blinks them on frame-counter bits, and our version latched them on a bitmask that ShowMilestones only ever sets to 0 or to a single index.
STILL OPEN in boss.c: BossSpewCoins references lbl_801189E0 six times more than retail does, which is structural, and ProcessSpewItems reads one 0.1f retail does not.

hypothesis.statement: The `f32 Random(f32)` width defect is a CLASS, not a boss.c typo: eight TUs declare it correctly and two did not, and a prototype whose argument or return width disagrees with the definition changes which pool constant every call site loads while leaving the instruction words alone. Run tools/gdl/externcheck.py and tools/gdl/abicheck.py over the whole tree filtered to FLOAT-WIDTH disagreements only, and screen each hit with cr_datum_screen.py -- the two censuses that already exist rank type-class conflicts, and neither ranks the ones that change a pool datum.
